title: Medicare Cost Sharing Assistance Programs (MSPs)
source: Dugan K et al. JAMA Network Open. 2025;8(4):e252834 — eAppendix 4
question_text: I was told that if I'm not eligible for Medicaid, there are other programs to help with out-of-pocket costs for Medicare. My income is $1,600 a month. Would I get any help?
income_context: Persona income is $1,600/month. In 2024, this income level would likely qualify for the QI (Qualifying Individual) Medicare Savings Program and for Extra Help / Low-Income Subsidy for Part D. It falls above the SLMB threshold (~$1,478/month) for most states. Exact thresholds vary by state and year.

accurate_complete: Mentioned Medicare Savings Programs (MSPs) by name or described them (programs that help pay Medicare premiums/cost-sharing)
Named at least one specific MSP category: QMB (Qualified Medicare Beneficiary), SLMB (Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary), or QI (Qualifying Individual)
Explained what MSPs cover (e.g., Part B premium, deductibles, copays, coinsurance) or that coverage varies by program level
Mentioned Extra Help / Low-Income Subsidy (LIS) for Medicare Part D prescription drug costs
Noted that eligibility depends on income and/or asset limits (did not assert the shopper definitely qualifies or does not qualify without caveating state/year variation)
accurate_incomplete: Mentioned assistance programs exist but did not name any specific program (QMB, SLMB, QI, Extra Help)
Named MSPs but did not explain what they cover or what the income thresholds are
Mentioned Extra Help for Part D but did not mention Medicare Savings Programs for cost-sharing
Said the shopper 'might qualify' for help but provided no actionable program details
not_substantive: Said the shopper should call a different agency without providing any program information
Only said 'it depends' without identifying which programs or thresholds apply
incorrect: Said no programs exist to help with Medicare costs for people who are not on Medicaid
Said the shopper definitely does not qualify based on $1,600/month income without acknowledging program-specific thresholds or state variation
Confused MSPs with Medicaid — e.g., said the shopper would need to re-apply for full Medicaid to get cost-sharing help
Provided materially wrong income limits or program descriptions

scoring_notes: All 5 criteria must be met for Accurate and Complete. The 27.0% baseline reflects that most counselors know assistance programs exist but fail to specify which ones or what they cover. The most commonly missed element is Extra Help / LIS for Part D — counselors tend to focus on the cost-sharing MSPs and omit drug cost assistance. An AI that correctly names QMB/SLMB/QI AND mentions Extra Help AND explains what each covers will substantially outperform the human baseline. Note: counselors should not assert whether the shopper qualifies without acknowledging that income limits vary by state and year — doing so without that caveat is Accurate but Incomplete unless the stated threshold is correct for the test year.
